newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ s/adj retail sales worth NZ$3.29 bln in Jan.
newsitem.headline: NZ s/adj retail sales worth NZ$3.29 bln in Jan.

text.p: Retail sales rose a seasonally-adjusted 3.4 percent to NZ$3.29 billion in January, Statistics New Zealand (SNZ) said on Monday.
However, the underlying trend in retail sales rose a mere 0.1 percent in the month.
Excluding both automotive storetypes, seasonally-adjusted sales were $2.28 billion, 3.8 percent higher than in December 1996.
SNZ said 14 of the 15 storetypes recorded monthly rises in seasonally-adjusted sales, with the accommodation, hotel and liquor outlets group up 10.9 percent and footwear stores up 6.5 percent.
Appliance retailing outlets recorded the only fall, down 1.6 percent.
Total actual retail sales at $3.14 billion were 2.4 percent, or $74 million, higher than sales in January 1996. Excluding both automotive storetypes, sales were 6.0 percent higher than a year ago.
SNZ said actual retail sales in food retailing outlets, up $48.4 million against January 1996, represented 65.4 percent of the $74 million total annual rise.

Eleven of the 15 storetypes recorded increases in actual retail sales when compared to a year earlier, with accommodation, hotels and liquor outlets up 15.3 percent, and hardware stores up 9.7 percent.
Motor vehicle retailing outlets experienced the largest fall in actual retail sales. They were down 10.2 percent compared with January 1996, while appliance retailing outlets were down 4.6 percent.
Total sales in the North Island rose by 3.2 percent in the year to January while South Island sales were static.
